dispositions.method: The automatic families first printed in 1774 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json: 692 items found on the pages, 259 in 4 or more papers by the finder's count), and again with the families of 1773 over the 1774 pages (items_from_1773.json: 23 items, none in 4 or more). Every item in 3 or more papers was compared by machine with every page and counted again by its opening; a sweep of seven-word sequences shared by 4 or more papers found 2,025 passages in 775 runs, and the runs no finder item covers were read (184 at first; after a fault in the first coverage check was fixed on 24 November, 122 runs are uncovered, all read). Counted item by item, 214 items meet the bar (count_1774.md). Every eligible item within two papers of the papers that survive for its weeks was searched for in the missing papers; the admitted and chosen items were counted with phrase searches over all 1,205 pages in both transcriptions and read on every page.
dispositions.selection_rule: The thin-year rule (Y-THIN, as amended on 23 November 2026, the owner's choice B1): an item, counted by its own words, is eligible when it was printed by more than half of the newspapers that survive for its weeks (those with a surviving issue between its first and last printing, and at least in the three weeks from its first printing), and by at least 4; as in R-01, the eligible items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted, and the other eligible items are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news, about as many stories as a standard year (about 20 to 35); one affair's items as in X-1800-01; digests are not admitted; sub-stories (C-01), private persons (R-04) and the list of items read and not admitted (R-03) as in every year. In 1774 5 to 7 papers survive for any item's weeks, so the bar is 4 papers for every item.
dispositions.paper_counting: 1774 has 8 catalogue series, which are 7 papers (C-04): the Connecticut Courant is sn82016376 to 24 May and sn82016139 (The Connecticut Courant and Hartford Weekly Intelligencer) from 7 June. Five papers run all year; Rind's Virginia Gazette survives for 13 January and from 21 April; the Pennsylvania Journal for 27 July only. 5 to 7 papers are in print in any three weeks. No 1774 issue has a corrected date; the release's map lists 5 misfiled RevX pages, on which no admitted printing stands. The Courant to 31 May is dated by weeks and filed under the first date (X-1774-12).

counted_item_by_item.Joins made by the finder: The finder joins the county and town resolves through their shared formulas ('the town of Boston is now suffering in the common cause of America'), the Congress's papers through the list of the colonies, and the acts of Parliament through the titles that later documents recite; each text was counted by its own words.

counted_item_by_item.The Congress's resolves of 8 October: Two printed forms counted together (C-02), printed again counts again (C-08): 5 papers, 7 printings; Rind's printing not counted (X-1774-05).
counted_item_by_item.Bills and acts: The two bills for Massachusetts Bay are counted as bills; the act for regulating the government as passed (1 paper) apart (X-1774-06).
counted_item_by_item.Acts printed whole: The Port Act (5) and the Quebec Act (4) are counted where printed whole from their titles; recitals and abstracts are not counted (X-1774-07).
